description: Hand-made cards (compiler input, scripts/compile-legends.mjs): notable players of 1997–2026 the source lacks in a title, cannot tell apart, or describes so thinly (national squads of leagues the game did not have, FIFA 98/99 keepers) that the measured card says nothing. `overall` is a judgement — from his other cards, his team-mates and his standing at the time; position, skills (moved to that overall like any card), foot and club come from the row named in `like` (`person` + `edition`: his own row under another id or in another title), or from his own row of that title. `person` is the EA id the card belongs to (FIFA 98/99's own ids are 98,000,000 + id / 99,000,000 + id), `edition` the title (98, 99, 0–26), `sourceName` a word of the name in the row used — the build fails when it does not match. These cards are marked in the provenance (data/build/eras.json stats.handCards) and never count towards a title's level.

cards.name: Gary Neville
cards.why: FIFA 98/99 list two 'Neville' at Manchester United and England and cannot say which is Gary: the right-back's row is his. England's right-back at the 1998 World Cup, a regular of the 1999 Treble side — level with his 2000–02 cards.

cards.name: Enzo Francescoli
cards.why: Only in FIFA 98, in Uruguay's squad: no card. South American Footballer of the Year 1995, River Plate's 1996 Libertadores and 1997 Supercopa in his last seasons, at 36.

cards.name: Dragan Stojković
cards.why: In the game only in Yugoslavia's squad (he played in Japan), rated 72: the captain and No. 10 of the 1998 World Cup side, J.League MVP.

cards.name: Hong Myung-bo
cards.why: Korea's sweeper at four World Cups; the K-League and J.League are barely described (70).

cards.name: Hong Myung-bo
cards.why: Bronze Ball of the 2002 World Cup, captain of the semi-finalists: FIFA 2003 has him at 73.

cards.name: Andreas Köpke
cards.why: Germany's No. 1 at Euro 96 (IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper 1996) and the 1998 World Cup: FIFA 98/99 have no keeper skills and the pooling leaves him at 81, behind three German keepers.

cards.name: Gianluca Pagliuca
cards.why: Italy's keeper at the 1998 World Cup, Inter's in the 1998 UEFA Cup win: his FIFA 98/99 row (Inter) is not tied to his later id (Bologna) and has no keeper skills.

cards.name: Andriy Shevchenko
cards.why: Dynamo Kyiv's 1997–99: the hat-trick at Camp Nou, the Champions League's top scorer and semi-finalist of 1998–99. FIFA 99 has him at Dynamo under an id of its own, pooled to 77.

cards.name: Serhiy Rebrov
cards.why: Shevchenko's partner at Dynamo Kyiv, Ukrainian Footballer of the Year 1996 and 1998; as Shevchenko, an untied FIFA 99 row.

cards.name: Mohamed Aboutrika
cards.why: The Egyptian league is not in the game before FIFA 12 (where he is 77, at 33): Africa's best home-based player, the Cup of Nations of 2006, Al Ahly's Champions Leagues and Club World Cup bronze.

cards.name: Mohamed Aboutrika
cards.why: The winning goal of the 2008 Cup of Nations final, BBC African Footballer of the Year 2008, second for the African award.

cards.name: Mohamed Al-Deayea
cards.why: Saudi Arabia's keeper at three World Cups, Asia's goalkeeper of the century (IFFHS): in the game only in the national squad, with no card.

cards.name: Saeed Al-Owairan
cards.why: Asian Footballer of the Year 1994 (the goal against Belgium), in Saudi Arabia's 1998 World Cup squad: national squad only, 74.

cards.name: Ali Daei
cards.why: Asian Footballer of the Year 1999, Bayern's striker in 1998–99, the record international scorer of his time: 78.

cards.name: Ümit Davala
cards.why: Two goals for third-placed Türkiye at the 2002 World Cup, Milan's and Inter's wing-back: FIFA 2002/03 list him twice and rate him 72.

cards.name: Edmundo
cards.why: Brazil's player of 1997 (a record 29 league goals for Vasco, Bola de Ouro), in the 1998 World Cup squad: only FIFA 98/99 know him, pulled to the titles' average (78).

cards.name: Alexi Lalas
cards.why: The face of United States soccer in the 1990s, in the 1998 World Cup squad: national squad only, under an id no later title ties to him.

cards.name: Eric Wynalda
cards.why: The United States' record scorer of the time, at his third World Cup in 1998: as Lalas.

cards.name: Maxi Rodríguez
cards.why: Argentina’s right midfielder at the 2006 World Cup (three goals, the volley against Mexico), Atlético’s captain: the source’s FIFA 04–07 extract (36 outfielders per nationality) leaves him out; FIFA 08 has him at 76, FIFA 09 at 82.

cards.name: Peter Crouch
cards.why: Started three of England’s matches at the 2006 World Cup after eleven goals for England that year, Liverpool’s centre-forward: missing from the FIFA 06/07 extract; FIFA 08 has him at 76, FIFA 10 at 79.

cards.name: Jérôme Boateng
cards.why: Started four matches of third-placed Germany at the 2010 World Cup at 21 (Hamburg, then Manchester City): the source has him from FIFA 12 (78) only.

cards.name: Egidio Arévalo Ríos
cards.why: The ball-winner of the 2010 semi-finalists in every match, then of the 2011 Copa América winners: Peñarol is not in FIFA 10/11; FIFA 13 has him at 77.

cards.name: Richard Kingson
cards.why: Ghana’s keeper to the 2010 quarter-final (and at the 2006 World Cup): the source has one row of him, FIFA 07 at 67.

cards.name: Yasser Al-Qahtani
cards.why: Saudi Arabia’s captain and scorer at the 2006 World Cup, Asian Footballer of the Year 2007: the Saudi league enters the game with FIFA 13 (74, at 30).

cards.name: Hamad Al-Montashari
cards.why: Asian Footballer of the Year 2005, Saudi Arabia’s centre-back at the 2006 World Cup: in the game from FIFA 13 (69, at 31).

cards.name: Mohammed Al-Shalhoub
cards.why: Saudi Arabia’s playmaker of the 2000s, in the 2006 World Cup squad: in the game from FIFA 13 (74, at 32).

cards.name: Sami Al-Jaber
cards.why: Scored at his fourth World Cup in 2006, Saudi Arabia’s record scorer: last in the game in FIFA 2003’s national squad (71).

cards.name: Nawaf Al-Temyat
cards.why: Asian Footballer of the Year 2000, in Saudi Arabia’s 2006 midfield: last in the game in FIFA 2002/03’s national squad.

cards.name: Mohamed Al-Deayea
cards.why: In his fourth World Cup squad in 2006 (178 caps): only FIFA 2000/01’s national squad has him (skills from the FIFA 2001 row).

cards.name: Mabrouk Zaid
cards.why: Saudi Arabia’s keeper in all three matches of 2006, Asian champion with Al-Ittihad in 2004 and 2005: in the game from FIFA 13 (65, at 33).

cards.name: Redha Tukar
cards.why: Saudi Arabia’s centre-back at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups: only FIFA 2003’s national squad has him.

cards.name: Ahmed Dokhi
cards.why: Saudi Arabia’s right-back at the 2006 World Cup: only the national squads of FIFA 98–2003 have him.

cards.name: Saud Khariri
cards.why: Saudi Arabia’s holding midfielder at the 2006 World Cup: in the game from FIFA 13 (69).
